mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong housing starts (HOUST above 1600 thousand units) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.7%) indicates robust consumer demand supported by accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: demand-driven expansion with loose monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where both HOUST > 1600 and FEDFUNDS < 0.7%.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion phases characterized by strong GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth above 2.0%), consumer demand is robust and corporate earnings are resilient, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with GDPC1 quarterly growth above 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO above 102.0) indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO is above 102.0.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeds 0.5% growth, it signals a rapidly strengthening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong consumer credit (RSAFS above 480,000 million dollars) and rising housing starts (HOUST above 1600 thousand units) indicates robust consumer demand and housing market activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where both RSAFS > 480000 and HOUST > 1600.
